title: Sovereignty Mode: Orchestrated VPC Residency Controller with Tamper-Evident Switchover Evidence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a controller and evidence pipeline that enforces VPC/on-prem data residency constraints during controlled regional switchover, produces tamper-evident cryptographic evidence bundles, and exposes machine-readable residency claims for legal/audit consumption. This ticket covers the residency decision engine, a 'soft-lock' holdback window for automated switchover, signed evidence artifacts (COSE/JSON-LD signed), and integration points for Console, Dedicated, and Private control planes.
acceptance_criteria: Controller enforces residency policy: requests flagged for 'sovereign-only' never leave configured region unless explicit operator override recorded
Switchover occurs only after soft-lock holdback window (configurable) and operator confirmation or pre-authorized emergency rule
Evidence bundle generated for every region change attempt: timestamped, signed by control-plane KMS, and containing resource hashes, routing decisions, and telemetry refs
Evidence bundles are exportable via API and archived to customer-controlled S3/GCS with integrity verification
Automated tests validate policy precedence, forced-switchover guardrails, and evidence verification logic
Console UI shows residency claim with proof link and last-signed timestamp
Backward-compatible: hosted customers without Private contracts get denied-at-policy enforcement, with clear error codes and remediation steps
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag behind 'sovereigntyController' on staging clusters; run synthetic traffic with residency flags. Phase 2: Canary to 5 customers in Private beta with audit team present. Phase 3: Gradual enable for Dedicated reservations, gated by successful evidence verification. Emergency rollback via feature flag and KMS revocation if signed evidence integrity fails.
implementation_notes: Design controller as a Kubernetes operator for Private/VPC deployments and a service-side module for hosted control plane
Evidence format: JSON-LD + COSE signature using customer-specific KMS key where available, else control-plane KMS with customer notification
Soft-lock window default: 300 seconds, configurable per-customer policy; purpose is to allow operator review and automated preflight checks
Policy precedence: explicit customer residency > account-level default > global default; document conflict resolution behavior
Telemetry: emit residency.decision, residency.attempt, residency.signed_evidence events with correlation id to tracing
Fallback behavior: if signing fails, abort switchover and surface diagnostics to operators and end-customer via audit API
QA_steps: Unit tests for policy engine: priority rules and override paths
Integration test: simulate locked region, inject capacity loss, verify controller blocks or requires approval
End-to-end: enable feature flag, initiate controlled switchover, verify evidence bundle signed and uploaded, validate signature using exported public key
Chaos test: randomly drop control plane connectivity during soft-lock window and verify safe-stall behavior
Compliance test: run evidence export against sample legal template and verify fields required by SOC2/GDPR checks are present
